About Liset

Liset Quezada is a small-town girl who was born and raised in San Luis Obispo, California. As the daughter of immigrants, her family background has shaped her commitment to protecting all people and ensuring that every community has a voice in government.

Quezada attended Claremont McKenna College, where she majored in Political Science and minored in Public Relations. Her education helped her develop a strong understanding of government, public policy, and political communication.

In 2024, Quezada served as a Campaign Outreach Intern for Kamala Harris’s presidential campaign. In this role, she helped with voter outreach, community engagement, and sharing campaign information with local communities. This experience introduced her to political organizing and strengthened her interest in public service.

Although Quezada has not yet held an elected office, her campaign experience and educational background have helped prepare her for a future in public service. Growing up as the daughter of immigrants influenced her political beliefs, particularly her commitment to protecting immigrant families, promoting equal opportunities, and ensuring that everyone is treated fairly under the law.

Quezada believes that a person’s background should never prevent them from feeling safe, being represented, or pursuing their dreams. Her experiences have inspired her to advocate for inclusive policies and a government that serves all people.

Campaign Speech

Watch the speech

Hello and good morning, my fellow Americans. My name is Liset Quezada, and I am honored to stand before you all today, accepting my nomination as a Democratic presidential candidate in this 2026 election. I am not another out-of-touch politician disconnected from the realities of everyday life, preaching how to solve your problems while never living through the struggles, wondering how to make a paycheck stretch another week.

I know struggle because I’ve lived it. My upbringing wasn’t as privileged as the rest; I am a proud daughter of immigrants who came here with big dreams and little money in their pockets. As I grew up, they taught me the value of a hard-earned dollar through long hours of work and sacrifice, proving that nothing in life is given, but it’s earned with resilience and honest work.

I’ve worked since I was 14 to help push my family towards financial stability. I know what it means for working families to hustle every day to make ends meet, which is why I am running for president; now more than ever, our country needs a leader who fights for the American people and not just for the best interests of money-hungry corporations and the ultra-wealthy.

My vision for America is a nation where housing is affordable and an honest day's work is enough to guarantee you a safe home, an America where there is an abundance of jobs and educational opportunities, quality affordable healthcare, and a secure future not just for us but for future generations to come.

Currently, our working class is posed with an existential threat: the use of artificial intelligence. With a rapidly developing technological society, if left unchecked, artificial intelligence will threaten the backbone of the economy by replacing real humans with software, and corporations will employ fewer people. As president, I will enforce strict regulations on the use of AI in the workforce in order to protect American workers. Without work, families will lose their stability and face financial hardships that will spiral into homelessness, with thousands of vulnerable people forced onto the streets in need of support. Every person deserves the opportunity to make an honest living.

To address the cost of living, I will create larger first-time homebuyer programs with lower interest rates, making housing more affordable and payments more manageable. I will enforce DEI initiatives across all institutions so everyone has equal opportunities. I will also make healthcare affordable. The first step to this would be to tax the top 1% to contribute their share in taxes.

And when it comes to gun control, we shouldn't have to choose between protecting our community and upholding the Constitution. We could still respect this amendment by implementing safeguards, keeping firearms out of the hands of convicted felons and People who have been checked into mental facilities.

At the end of the day, this campaign is about YOU; it’s about the working families who keep this country moving. I know what it’s like to work from the bottom up and how hard it is to earn every dollar, which is why I will never back down when fighting for your jobs, your family, and your future. Voting for Liset Quezada is voting for a government that will work as hard as you do. Thank you.

Why Vote

Reason 4: Gun Control Regulations

Stricter gun laws to reduce gun violence and keep people safe.

Reason 5: Support Working Families

Help families afford everyday necessities, and achieve financial stability.

Reason 6: More Jobs and Education

Expand job opportunities and access to education for the people.
